comparison: Both strongly support the census numbers (C1-C19, C69). OpenEval emphasizes the explicit numerical data and methodology transparency. Peer reviewers accept these numbers without question, with Reviewer 3 calling it 'a very useful resource.' Peer review also includes context claims (C70-C74) about repository sizes that OpenEval addresses separately in R23.

Both support claims about zip archives (C5, C83-C85). OpenEval focuses on the 7:1 ratio and logical limitations. Peer review accepts these technical observations and includes additional methodological claims (C139-C140, C193-C197) about handling zip archives that OpenEval addresses separately in R18 and R22.

Perfect agreement on temporal trends (C20-C25). Both accept the data deposition patterns and the hypothesis about Zenodo's preference. Peer reviewers note the analysis is 'presented clearly and discussed insightfully.'

Perfect agreement on file distribution by MD software (C26-C30). Both accept the Gromacs focus as appropriate for proof-of-concept. Reviewer 2 explicitly notes 'the study primarily focuses on one major MD engine (GROMACS), although this limitation is not significant.'

Both support trajectory file comparisons (C31-C37). OpenEval focuses on these specific claims. Peer review includes additional technical details about file formats (C38-C40, C86-C95) that OpenEval addresses separately in R6 and R29. Reviewer 3 explicitly notes the ~10k vs ~30k comparison.

Both support .xtc file analysis (C38-C40, C95). OpenEval emphasizes the sampling strategy and extreme case citation. Peer review groups these with broader trajectory analysis. The technical details are accepted without challenge.

Both support system size analysis (C41-C45). OpenEval emphasizes the range and enrichment explanation. Peer review also includes hypotheses about water removal (C96-C98) that OpenEval addresses separately in R30. Analysis is 'presented clearly and discussed insightfully.'

Both support molecular composition findings (C46-C47, C99-C103). OpenEval emphasizes the NMRLipids hypothesis. Peer review also includes implications (C104-C106) that OpenEval addresses separately in R31. Reviewers accept characterizations as 'useful snapshot.'

Strong agreement on diverse molecular systems (C48, C107-C116). OpenEval emphasizes breadth with citations. Peer review notes materials sciences are 'severely under-represented' but accepts this reflects Gromacs user community. Also includes C117 that OpenEval addresses in R31.

Perfect agreement on topology files (C49-C51, C118-C119). Both accept the explicit numbers and inference about information content. Reviewer 3 notes the work reveals 'potential hidden treasures of MD simulations and force field parametrizations.'

Perfect agreement on reusability-enabling files (C52-C53, C120-C122). Both accept the file counts and potential for rerunning simulations. Reviewer 3 notes the work reveals 'the high value of these data' for potential reuse.

Strong agreement on simulation parameters (C54-C59, C124-C125). OpenEval emphasizes explicit numbers and coarse-grain criteria. Peer review also includes C123 (OpenEval R36). Reviewer 3 praises analyzing 'how researchers *actually* run simulations' as 'much better than analyzing what authors write in Methods sections.'

Perfect agreement on thermostat/barostat usage (C60-C62, C126-C128). Both accept the patterns and explanations for files without these controls. Reviewer 3's praise about analyzing actual simulation practices applies here as well.

Perfect agreement on temperature distributions (C63-C66, C129-C130). Both accept the ranges and explanations for specific temperature peaks. The findings are consistent with expected simulation practices.

Strong agreement on data sharing tools (C67-C68, C131-C134). OpenEval emphasizes concrete deliverables. Peer review also includes visualization details (C208-C209) from OpenEval R21. All reviewers explicitly praise the MDverse data explorer as 'a very useful tool.'

Both support metadata quality issues (C75-C79, C154-C155). OpenEval emphasizes these motivated the Ex² strategy. Peer review also includes limitation acknowledgments (C138, C149) and metadata enrichment strategies (C156-C157). Reviewers accept these as key motivation for the work.

Reviewer 3 praises the 'novel search strategy' as 'likely to have many true positives and few false positives.'
